memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord said to Moses, 'Come up to me on the mountain and stay here, and I will give you the tablets of stone with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.'" - Exodus 24:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls Moses higher up the mountain, promising to give him tablets of stone containing commandments that God Himself had written. Notice the emphasis: these were not Moses' ideas or a nation's invented traditions. God says, "I have written." These words came from God's own hand, for the instruction of His people.

This matters enormously. The law was not a human construction meant to control people; it was divine revelation meant to guide them. God gave His people something solid and enduring — words on stone rather than shifting opinions. When we open Scripture today, we are not reading merely the thoughts of ancient men, but words God breathed out for our teaching, correction, and training (2 Tim 3:16).

Notice too the invitation: "Come up to me on the mountain and stay here." God did not simply mail the tablets down. He called Moses into His presence and told him to remain. God's Word is best received in God's presence, not merely as information gathered but as truth received from a Person. When you open the Bible, remember that you are being invited up the mountain to meet with God Himself. Come, and stay a while.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I approach Scripture as God's own words, or merely as ancient human writing?
Am I willing to "come up and stay" — to linger in God's presence rather than rush?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Scripture is Your own Word given for my instruction. When I open it, draw me up into Your presence and help me linger there with You. Amen.
